T: Old pines. Somebody carved an open hand into one of them, a very long time ago.
M: The Broken Watch: a Hale watchtower. The horde never used it. A raider once said it was 'too polite'.
E: The tower door, wedged shut with five hundred years of ivy and one very stubborn broom.
j: A cairn. On the top stone, a little open hand, carved by someone who wanted it to last.
G: A road-block of sharpened stakes, very new, very pointy, and nowhere near the road. Grub put it up himself.
^: The road north, back to the tithe camps.
_: The road south. Past the trees, banners stand in a field, hundreds of them.

objects.name: Watchman Orrin
lines: Halt! Who goes— oh. A visitor. We don't get visitors. We get weather.
Orrin, of the Watch. My family's kept this tower nineteen generations. We're waiting to be relieved.
Nobody's come yet. Any day now, I expect.

answer: By the king's men. The old king. Hale. The one with the open hand.
My great-great-…-great-grandad was told: hold the watch till you're relieved. So we hold it.
The horde says there's a new king. We don't recognise him. He hasn't sent a relief.
The Field of Banners. Where the last battle was meant to be. Every army in the world, meant to meet there.
They never did. Something stopped it. My family wrote it down: 'Day of the Field. Nobody came. Strange quiet. Ate lunch.'

lines: News came up the road. The king's been beaten. Challenged, fair, by the old law.
Does that count as being relieved? I've been thinking about it all morning. I think I'll wait a bit longer. Just to be sure.

objects.name: Grub
lines: What's south? Dunno. Never been. King's orders.
I've stood here three years. I've got very good at standing.
King got beaten, they're saying. So the orders are… nobody's sure.
Go on, then. South. I'll stand here anyway. I'm good at it.
A Hale waystone, the open hand carved at the top.
THE FIELD OF BANNERS, SOUTH. MAY NO ONE EVER NEED IT.
